a: ‘Al-‘adiyat’: the running horses, as they gallop in His way toward the enemy.
The ‘dabh’ of horses: the sound of their breaths within them while running.
‘Those striking sparks’: the horses that strike the stones with their hooves, so sparks fly from them.
‘Those striking sparks’: the horses that strike the stones with their hooves, so sparks fly from them.
At the beginning of the day.
And they stirred up and spread.
‘And penetrated therewith into a host’: they went with their riders into the midst of the enemy’s hosts.
‘Jam‘’: a group of people; what is meant is the hosts of the enemy.
A particle of emphasis and of the accusative, conveying emphasis of the content of the sentence.
The male and the female of the children of Adam.
To his God who is worshipped.
‘Inna’: a particle of emphasis and of the accusative, conveying emphasis of the content of the sentence.
A preposition conveying the meaning of figurative superposition.
A demonstrative for the distant masculine singular; one person is addressed with it.
‘Inna’: a particle of emphasis and of the accusative, conveying emphasis of the content of the sentence.
‘Love of good’: the inclination of the soul toward it.
‘Al-khayr’: a means of benefit and welfare, such as wealth and horses.
Surely strong, diligent in acquiring it, avidly devoted to it.
‘Ala’: a particle that comes here for urging.
An adverb that indicates, in most cases, future time.
Stirred up, brought out, and scattered.
A preposition conveying the meaning of literal spatial containment.
Plural of ‘qabr’; a person’s qabr is the place of his burial.
‘What is in the breasts is obtained’: what was hidden in the breasts of good or evil is made manifest and gathered for the reckoning.
A preposition conveying the meaning of figurative containment.
Plural of sadr; the sadr of a human is the part extending from the bottom of the neck to the space of the cavity; in the Qur’an it is applied to the heart because of its being in it.
A particle of emphasis and of the accusative, conveying emphasis of the content of the sentence.
‘Ba’: a preposition conveying the meaning of adherence (attachment).

‘Khabir’: an attribute of Allah, glorified and exalted; al-Khabir is the One acquainted with the reality of things, so nothing hidden is hidden from Allah; He knows the universals and the particulars, and whoever denies that has disbelieved.
